notes.text: The author opens “Je veux revenir” and says condition b) can be made much more precise by using the information in the preceding number. No authorial page number is visible at the top. A small, lighter-hand 51 appears at the lower left and is transcribed as that hand’s foliation, without assigning it to the author.

In b_1 the author describes a bijective correspondence between the points z_alpha above x and germs B_alpha of bordering subspaces at x, and describes these germs as images under the underlined map-name b. The compressed superscript after the first equality remains unresolved; body occurrences visibly have the left-angle form. The connecting shaft under b remains explicitly doubtful.

In b_2 the author writes n=card({z_alpha}) and asserts existence and uniqueness of a point x-tilde with the specified n images. He then states that there is a natural total-order structure on the level-1 strata B_alpha passing through x. The word total and the phrase dans Sigma^{<}(0)=Sigma are insertions. The marginal diagram has three labelled arrows, two written vertical dots, tilded endpoints and a star at its target; its source exponent is unresolved.

In b_3 the live lower bound is visibly 1≤d, with a separate lower bar. The author associates the displayed map with the written inclusion expression {d} subset {0,1,--,d}, then describes correspondences with subsets of cardinal d and begins the description using an increasing map from Delta_d={0,--d}. The page ends at en. These are accounts of the manuscript’s claims, not proof checks.

The wording on the first subset line is de un, with two written words. It is preserved. The end reads en associant : à telle partie A, without une. The insertions imm and str have no visible separate final stops. The cancelled form before the live z_alpha in b_2 has B-like lobes and is retained as B_alpha|z_alpha in doubt. No mathematical theorem or expected argument was used to supply a missing word, sign, digit or endpoint.
